sample_unit: CTPA exams flagged by AI as suspected PE
models_evaluated: FDA-approved PE AI algorithm (CTPA PE detection and RV/LV ratio)

links.outcome: False positive rate of AI PE detection on local CTPA versus radiologist report
links.effect: 57 of 200 exams (28.5%) correctly positive; 143 (71.5%) incorrectly positive; false positive rate 71.5% versus prior validation of 91% sensitivity, 100% specificity.
links.quote: The false positive rate of our AI algorithm was 71.5%, higher than what was reported in the AI's prior clinical validity study (91% sensitivity, 100% specificity).

links.outcome: Alert burden and notification fatigue from AI auto-detection notifications to PERT
links.effect: High rate of discordant AI auto-detection (71.5% false positives) raised concerns of increased PERT workload, alarm/notification fatigue, and automation bias; direct notification did not improve PERT triage efficacy.
links.quote: This can lead to increased workloads for PERT consultants, alarm/notification fatigue, and automation bias.

screen.reason: This empirical study evaluates the clinical validity, real-world false positive rate, and PERT workflow impact of an FDA-approved AI tool deployed for pulmonary embolism detection, but it does not compare outcomes with and without a specific deployment safeguard or practice.
